Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

Emerald Foundation, Inc., awarded $300,000 to support research harnessing natural killer (NK) cells for use in immunotherapies. NK cells play a major role in the elimination of both tumors and infected cells, and this research will provide valuable insight that will inform better treatment strategies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hard-to-treat cancers are focus of Cancer Research Institute grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Research Institute (CRI) has awarded nearly $1.5 million in grants to Dana-Farber in support of investigations into how immunotherapy can be used to defeat difficult-to-treat and incurable cancers

jetpack-related-posts.title: Tricking the immune system to defeat cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The New York Stem Cell Foundation (NYSCF) awarded a five-year, $1.5 million grant to Dana-Farber’s Judith Agudo, PhD, for her work to make cancerous tumors more susceptible to immunotherapies and to protect transplanted organs from attack by the immune system.

img.alt_text: The New York Stem Cell Foundation Research Institute logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Samuel Waxman Cancer Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Samuel Waxman Cancer Research Foundation awarded $200,000 to Dana-Farber to support research into how aging affects the behavior of tumor cells. This research, led by Lewis Cantley, PhD, in the Department of Cancer Biology, could provide further insight that may inform the development of age-specific treatment approaches for cancer.

img.alt_text: Liquid pouring from a beaker into a petri dish

jetpack-related-posts.title: CRI grants accelerate immunotherapy research at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Research Institute (CRI) is advancing bold new strategies to harness the immune system against cancer through two grants at DanaFarber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance advances personalized immunotherapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $900,000 Team Science grant will advance collaboration and innovation in immunotherapies for melanoma at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defeating treatment-resistant lung cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A collaborative, multi-institution team led by Dana-Farber’s David Barbie, MD, received a four-year, $2.5 million grant from the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) and Lung Cancer Research Foundation (LCRF) for researching a cure for non-small cell lung carcinoma.

img.alt_text: IASLC Lung Cancer Research Foundation logo

title.rendered: A Celebration for the Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology Chair at Dana-Farber

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Justin Knight

Supporters gathered to celebrate the recently established Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology Chair at Dana-Farber. The endowed Chair was funded by colleagues, mentees, grateful patients, family, and friends in honor of Robert J. Mayer, MD, who served as director of the Fellowship Program for more than 35 years. Ann LaCasce, MD, MMSc, who succeeded Mayer as director, was appointed the first incumbent. Pictured (from left): Mayer, LaCasce, and Dana-Farber President and CEO Laurie H. Glimcher, MD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In October, Dana-Farber supporters and leaders gathered for the annual Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium. Attendees received firsthand updates on the State of the Institute, advances and opportunities in prevention and early detection, the impact of philanthropy on advancing research, and Dana-Farber’s world-renowned hematology/oncology fellowship program. Pictured are fellowship program…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Supporting the next generation of physician-scientists
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For 50 years, Dana-Farber’s Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology has attracted the brightest early career physicians, researchers, and nurse-scientists to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in their pursuit of specialized training opportunities in cancer medicine.

img.alt_text: A close-up photo of two people outside

jetpack-related-posts.title: Physician pioneer in palliative care establishes a research fellowship
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2001, Janet L. Abrahm, MD, joined Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as a palliative care physician, becoming a pivotal force in founding and nurturing the Adult Palliative Care Program—a move that created a sea change in how Dana-Farber cares for patients with cancer and brought much-deserved attention and recognition to the field.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Creating community for adolescent and young adult patients
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each day, nearly 50 adolescent and young adult (AYA) patients—those between the ages of 15 and 39—come to Dana-Farber for treatment, but many never connect with one another because they wait for appointments on different floors.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Endowed fellowship looks to the future
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Baila Janock embodies generosity in its many forms. For over 30 years, she has combined her gifts of time, treasure, and talent to make a long-lasting impact on Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and its patients.

img.alt_text: Robert Mayer, MD, Baila Janock, and Janock Fellow Haley Ellis, MD

jetpack-related-posts.title: Poorvu Jaffe Chair Celebration
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: James Tulsky, MD, was named the first incumbent of the Poorvu Jaffe Chair in Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care at Dana-Farber, the first chair in this field established at the Institute. The Poorvu Jaffe Family’s gift also established the Poorvu Jaffe Fund for Supportive Oncology and Health Equity. Pictured at…

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

Richard and Eileen Greisch made a gift of $100,000 to provide essential resources for melanoma research under the direction of Tamara Sussman, MD. These funds will enable researchers to test novel therapeutics in clinical trials, lead investigations in genomic sequencing, and develop groundbreaking immunotherapeutic approaches.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robinson Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Robinson Family established the memorial Lena Maximo Robinson Fund with a $100,000 gift, supporting the melanoma research of F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. With these funds, Hodi’s team will continue their leadership in developing next-generation, cutting-edge treatments for all subtypes…

img.alt_text: Lena Maximo Robinson and Richard Robinson.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robert and Margaret King
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Robert and Margaret King made a gift of $100,000, supporting melanoma research under the direction of Megan Insco, MD, PhD. Their generous donation advances critical studies in the development of novel therapeutic approaches for the most difficult-to-treat melanomas, while enhancing clinical care for patients affected by this challenging disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor renewed their support for the O’Connor-MacGregor Fund for Melanoma Research with a new $150,000 commitment. This latest gift will support research into the underlying drivers of melanoma and development of durable therapeutic options under the direction of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jonathan and Hope Ashner
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A generous $100,000 gift from Jonathan and Hope Ashner was made to support the research of Elizabeth Buchbinder, MD. The gift will help to fuel Buchbinder’s groundbreaking investigations into melanoma and maximize progress against the disease.

img.alt_text: Steaming beaker and pipette in the lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jay and Kristy Ladieu
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jay and Kristy Ladieu gave $125,000 to support melanoma research under the direction of Megan Insco, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber. Fueled by this gift, Insco and her team are pursuing studies into the biology of melanoma, laying the groundwork for critically needed treatment options.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber donors Jay and Kristy Ladieu stop for a photo while on a bike ride

jetpack-related-posts.title: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor made a generous $100,000 commitment, renewing their support of melanoma research under the leadership of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD. Their impactful philanthropy is driving innovative studies in immunotherapy, including those targeting anti-tumor immunity, aiming to uncover new treatments and improve outcomes for melanoma patients worldwide.

img.alt_text: Three people in a Dana-Farber exam room

Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

The Holiday Patient Assistance Program, which helps patients and families in critical financial need, raised $192,785 in 2022. The program helped 726 eligible Dana-Farber patients and families celebrate the season by providing gift cards to help cover the cost of expenses like gas to travel to appointments, groceries for holiday meals, and small gifts for loved ones.

jetpack-related-posts.title: HomeGoods expands support to enhance patient care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Through HomeGoods’ Find Home Anywhere mission—funded largely by donations from its generous shoppers—HomeGoods and the TJX Foundation have made a three-year commitment to donate at least $3.6 million to Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Yawkey Foundation supports patients and staff
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 1953, Tom and Jean Yawkey initiated what would become a legacy of remarkable support by helping to establish the historic relationship between the Boston Red Sox, Sidney Farber, MD, and the Jimmy Fund.

img.alt_text: People pose for a photo in front of a food truck

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Yawkey Foundation’s heartfelt support
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Yawkey Foundation is a longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, stemming from the historic relationship between the Jimmy Fund and the Boston Red Sox. Perpetuating the philanthropic legacy of the team’s owners, Tom and Jean Yawkey, the foundation made gifts totaling $180,000 in 2024.

img.alt_text: Two people holding ice cream outside a Cookie Monstah food truck

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The success of our mission hinges on unrestricted gifts, including those raised through the Defy Cancer Fund.

jetpack-related-posts.title: One Mission
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One Mission recently demonstrated its commitment to cancer patients with two gifts totaling nearly $220,000 in support of the Blum Pediatric Resource Room and Pediatric Resource Program at Dana-Farber. One Mission, founded in 2008 by Ashley and Ari Haseotes, aims to help families cope with the emotional and financial challenges…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prado gift supports access for the underprivileged
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Institute Trustee Gary Prado and his wife, Darlene Prado, have established The Prado Family Impact Fund at Dana-Farber

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Jessamyn Martin

The 7th annual Jog for Julie fundraiser, held in honor of a breast cancer patient, raised more than $30,000 in 2022. The 5K was started in 2014 by Julie’s entire family, including her four children, and has raised more than $220,000 for breast cancer research at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: OOFOS surpasses $4 million milestone in 2024 to advance breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For nearly a decade, OOFOS has supported breast cancer research at Dana-Farber through its Project Pink initiative.

img.alt_text: Four people pose for a photo with Red Sox mascots at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast cancer patient inspires endowed fund at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Suzanne Michels Obenshain was 42 years old and living in Switzerland with her husband and three young children when she was diagnosed with stage IV triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

img.alt_text: Suzanne Michels Obenshain with her children on a ski trip

jetpack-related-posts.title: Keep Smiling Beautiful
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Keep Smiling Beautiful is a 5K race hosted by the family of Chelsea Smith, to champion research into hepatocellular carcinoma—liver cancer—by Chelsea’s doctor, Allison O’Neill, MD, at Dana-Farber. Each year, in Chelsea’s honor, O’Neill runs this 5K which has raised more than $115,000 since 2017.

img.alt_text: An image of a photo collage with balloons

jetpack-related-posts.title: OOFOS steps up for breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In fiscal year 2023, active recovery footwear brand OOFOS donated $626,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through their Project Pink initiative, a special program that supports breast cancer research by donating a percentage of online sales to the Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ninety Nine Restaurant & Pub
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For its 19th year, Ninety Nine Restaurant & Pub held its annual “Give $5, Get $5” fundraiser in 2024, donating 100% of the funds raised to support Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund. From August 12 to 25, guests who donated $5 received a $5 off coupon. The total exceeded $113,000…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Michael Swidler
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute received a gracious contribution from Michael Swidler to establish the Nancy Swidler Fund for Breast Cancer Research in honor of his late wife. Managed by Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, this fund is intended to advance pioneering breast cancer research and create pathways to better outcomes for every…

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Capehart Photography 

Institute Trustee Michele Kessler and her husband, Howard Kessler, made a gift of $250,000 to launch the Cannabis Care Support Program at Dana-Farber, which aims to create sustainable oncologic cannabis educational resources and advance research on the use of cannabis to address the mental and physical side effects of cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Kesslers’ vision for advancing AML research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Kesslers donated $1 million to advance AML research led by Robert Soiffer, MD, chief of the Division of Hematologic Malignancies and Worthington and Margaret Collette Professor of Medicine in the Field of Hematologic Oncology at Harvard Medical School. This substantial gift will empower Soiffer and his team to continue…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kesslers expedite research to expand treatment options for AML
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A crucial infusion of funds from Michele and Howard Kessler is enabling the clinical trial of a promising combination treatment.

img.alt_text: A couple poses for a photo in front of a flower display

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach surpasses $67 million in gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over three decades, the compassionate community in Palm Beach, Florida, has provided generous support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s lifesaving mission to conquer cancer in adults and children—not only in Boston and Palm Beach, but also across the country and around the world.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber Palm Beach Campaign Leadership Celebration Dinner

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign Cabinet
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Campaign Cabinet devoted their time, talents, and resources to advancing The Dana-Farber Campaign’s mission to Defy Cancer.

img.alt_text: Institute Trustees Michael Eisenson and Monica Chandra at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eisenson encourages CGAs as a simple and lasting legacy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Supporting cancer research and care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute can take many forms that benefit both the Institute and the donor. Michael Eisenson (pictured), Institute Trustee and chair of The Dana-Farber Campaign, recently established a charitable gift annuity (CGA) with a generous gift of $250,000.

img.alt_text: Michael Eisenson at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's healing garden

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Cox Family continues support of Dana-Farber’s revolutionary science
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Career venture capitalist and Institute Trustee Howard Cox and his wife, Wendy Cox, are no strangers to the revolutionary science and clinical treatments happening at the Institute.

Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

As part of their mission to fund innovative research at top institutions around the country, the Lymphoma Research Foundation’s recent funding cycle included awarding grants totaling $115,000 to fund two Dana-Farber studies into advanced treatment options for patients diagnosed with T-cell lymphoma and mantle cell lymphoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society attacks rare and resistant blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society (LLS) has awarded six grants totaling $5.8 million to Dana-Farber investigators.

img.alt_text: An artist’s rendering of bone marrow cells showing acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society grants target blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society recently awarded more than $7.3 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers in its quest to better understand and find cures for blood cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Conquering blood cancers is focus of Blood Cancer United grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year, nearly 200,000 Americans are diagnosed with leukemia, lymphoma, myeloma, or another bloodborne cancer. Blood Cancer United has awarded $4.2 million in grants to eight Dana-Farber physician-scientists working to better understand, treat, and potentially cure these often deadly diseases.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Magda And Gus Mininberg
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Magda and Gus Mininberg have made a generous $200,000 contribution to strengthen the Mininberg Family Fund for Cancer Research and the Mininberg Family Fund for Lymphoma Research, guided by David C. Fisher, MD. Their generosity provides steady, strategic support to Fisher and other Dana-Farber Cancer Institute leaders pursuing better outcomes…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lymphoma Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lymphoma Research Foundation awarded Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's Tianfang Ma, PhD, a generous $195,000 Postdoctoral Fellowship Grant, to bolster his research and growth as an independent investigator. Ma’s work focuses on the tumor immune microenvironment in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and may help enhance immunotherapy effectiveness and identify predictive markers…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lymphoma Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lymphoma Research Foundation gave $235,000 to support novel research in lymphoma led by Dana-Farber’s Christine Ryan, MD, and Mwanasha Merrill, MD. Both are focused on better understanding the underlying biology that drives the development and advancement of this disease, information which will translate into the delivery of more effective…

By Colleen Sullivan

jetpack-related-posts.title: Accelerating progress for adenoid cystic carcinoma
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Nearly two decades ago, Marnie Kaufman was diagnosed with adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC), a rare type of cancer most commonly arising in the salivary glands. Shortly thereafter, she and her husband, Jeff, established the Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma Research Foundation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Freedlander bequest focuses on inflammatory breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The estate of Ruth Freedlander made a $1.8 million bequest to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that will advance research into inflammatory breast cancer (IBC), a rare and aggressive disease that is particularly difficult to treat.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PHASE ONE Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PHASE ONE gave $273,768 to support Glenn Hanna, MD, who is leading a study to investigate a potential therapeutic target for a subgroup of adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) patients. This rare disease usually arises in the salivary glands, and there are currently no approved systemic therapies for advanced or metastatic…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arthur David Levin
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a gift of $100,000, Arthur David Levin established the Andrew John Torino Fund for Esophageal Cancer in honor of a dear friend’s husband, Andrew. This fund will advance the development of a new test to detect circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in the blood, with the goal of determining the…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defeating treatment-resistant lung cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A collaborative, multi-institution team led by Dana-Farber’s David Barbie, MD, received a four-year, $2.5 million grant from the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) and Lung Cancer Research Foundation (LCRF) for researching a cure for non-small cell lung carcinoma.

img.alt_text: IASLC Lung Cancer Research Foundation logo

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Joe Connolly gave $100,000 to fund critical small cell lung cancer research at Dana-Farber. Established in honor of Connolly’s late wife, the Deborah A. Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund is supporting Jacob Sands, MD, who in collaboration with Matthew Oser, MD, PhD, is exploring new methods to predict…

Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

The National Palliative Care Research Center awarded $198,000 to support the creation of a program to develop nurse-led psychosocial intervention for historically marginalized pediatric patients, with the goal of improving family-centered communication and pediatric patients’ quality of life during treatment.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Physician pioneer in palliative care establishes a research fellowship
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2001, Janet L. Abrahm, MD, joined Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as a palliative care physician, becoming a pivotal force in founding and nurturing the Adult Palliative Care Program—a move that created a sea change in how Dana-Farber cares for patients with cancer and brought much-deserved attention and recognition to the field.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leadership gift establishes Poorvu Jaffe Chair in Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care and launches health equity initiative
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber is committed to providing the best possible care to patients from all walks of life. In recent years, the Institute has prioritized expanding its clinical facilities into surrounding communities to better reach medically underserved patients with the Institute’s signature Total Patient Care model, which includes supportive services from the…

img.alt_text: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and Daniel G. Jaffe

jetpack-related-posts.title: William Randolph Hearst Foundations
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The William Randolph Hearst Foundations gave $200,000 to fund two one-year Nurse Practitioner Adult Palliative Care Fellowships at Dana-Farber, to support two nurse practitioners in the Department of Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care, where the focus on treating the whole person—mind, body, and spirit—helps provide patients with relief from the…

jetpack-related-posts.title: A legacy of care: Elevating palliative nursing education
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Shannon Robins and her husband, Jason Robins, co-founder and CEO of DraftKings, a Jimmy Fund corporate sponsor, made a visionary $1 million gift to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, helping to launch a first-of-its-kind palliative care education program designed by nurses, for nurses.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eliminating disparities to improve outcomes
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With philanthropic support from the Scarlet Feather Fund, Dana-Farber’s Kira Bona, MD, MPH, and Christopher Lathan, MD, MS, MPH, chief clinical access and equity officer and the Hadley Family Chair at Dana-Farber, are leading bold, innovative approaches that aim to reduce disparities in outcomes for adult and pediatric cancer patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society enables pathbreaking new inquiries
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Recent grants from the American Cancer Society fund innovative projects across Dana-Farber, from basic science to pediatric cancer disparities.

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor renewed their support for the O’Connor-MacGregor Fund for Melanoma Research with a new $150,000 commitment. This latest gift will support research into the underlying drivers of melanoma and development of durable therapeutic options under the direction of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor made a generous $100,000 commitment, renewing their support of melanoma research under the leadership of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD. Their impactful philanthropy is driving innovative studies in immunotherapy, including those targeting anti-tumor immunity, aiming to uncover new treatments and improve outcomes for melanoma patients worldwide.

img.alt_text: Three people in a Dana-Farber exam room

jetpack-related-posts.title: Blitzer renews support with generous new commitment to melanoma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Donor and patient advocate Michael Blitzer recently renewed his support of melanoma research at Dana-Farber with a $650,000 commitment.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robinson Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Robinson Family established the memorial Lena Maximo Robinson Fund with a $100,000 gift, supporting the melanoma research of F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. With these funds, Hodi’s team will continue their leadership in developing next-generation, cutting-edge treatments for all subtypes…

img.alt_text: Lena Maximo Robinson and Richard Robinson.

jetpack-related-posts.title: John Cassidy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: John Cassidy’s generous $300,000 gift establishes the Cassidy Family Melanoma Fellowship, to significantly advance melanoma research. Under the guidance of principal investigator F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber, this funding will help support the mentorship of an early career investigator, fostering innovation…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding in 2007, the Melanoma Research Alliance has become the largest nonprofit funder of crucial melanoma research worldwide. In 2025, they awarded $430,000 in grants to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporting the work of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD, Giacomo Oliveira, PhD, and David Liu, MD, MPH, MS, to advance…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kittredges continue generous support of melanoma and immuno-oncology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Francis Kittredge, MD, JD, and his wife, Adele, know that supporting Dana-Farber Cancer Institute makes a difference because their philanthropy already has—and their impact continues to grow through their ongoing generosity.

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Theresa Johnson Photography 

James Tulsky, MD, was named the first incumbent of the Poorvu Jaffe Chair in Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care at Dana-Farber, the first chair in this field established at the Institute. The Poorvu Jaffe Family’s gift also established the Poorvu Jaffe Fund for Supportive Oncology and Health Equity. Pictured at a celebration in November 2022 are (standing, from left) Dana-Farber President and CEO Laurie H. Glimcher, MD; Institute Trustee Alison Poorvu Jaffe and Daniel Jaffe; and Tulsky; (seated) Lia and Bill Poorvu.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber is committed to providing the best possible care to patients from all walks of life. In recent years, the Institute has prioritized expanding its clinical facilities into surrounding communities to better reach medically underserved patients with the Institute’s signature Total Patient Care model, which includes supportive services from the…

img.alt_text: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and Daniel G. Jaffe

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lawrence J. and Anne Rubenstein Charitable Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lawrence J. and Anne Rubenstein Charitable Foundation awarded a $380,000 grant to James A. Tulsky, MD, Dana-Farber’s Poorvu Jaffe Chair in Supportive Oncology, bolstering the Supportive Oncology Teams Initiative. This funding will accelerate efforts to integrate interdisciplinary teams into oncology care and enhance and improve quality of life for…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and Dan Jaffe support Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and her husband, Dan Jaffe, renewed their support for the Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center at Dana-Farber to help stem the disease’s dramatic rise among people under 50.

img.alt_text: Two people pose for a photo at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Physician pioneer in palliative care establishes a research fellowship
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2001, Janet L. Abrahm, MD, joined Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as a palliative care physician, becoming a pivotal force in founding and nurturing the Adult Palliative Care Program—a move that created a sea change in how Dana-Farber cares for patients with cancer and brought much-deserved attention and recognition to the field.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, honored with endowed chair
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A generous group of Trustees, colleagues, friends, and supporters contributed over $3 million to establish the chair and commemorate Glimcher’s legacy.

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

Over 30 streamers and content creators from around the U.S. participated in the latest Quest 2 Defy Cancer. The program, part of the Jimmy Fund Let’s Game® initiative, invites streamers, gamers, and content creators to make an impact on the lifesaving work happening at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Longest running Jimmy Fund fundraiser still going strong
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For more than 70 years, Showcase Cinemas has helped Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund defy cancer through the magic of the movies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Golf celebrates 40 years of defying cancer from the fairways
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun returned in full force in 2022, with courses around New England and across the country welcoming golfers in support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund’s lifesaving mission.

jetpack-related-posts.title: GivingTuesday inspires thousands to defy cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For many, Thanksgiving weekend marks the start of the holiday season, with family gatherings and a spirit of gratitude in the air. Since 2012, GivingTuesday celebrates this special time of year by encouraging charitable giving on the Tuesday after Black Friday and Cyber Monday shopping.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Celebrating our community fundraising heroes
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: At the heart of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund’s mission to defy cancer is a community making a difference–one dollar, one event, and one story at a time.

img.alt_text: Family of four in front of a Dustin Strong poster

jetpack-related-posts.title: Giving Day celebrates 75 years of progress
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 22, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund held its fourth annual Giving Day—an inspirational day of hope, where supporters come together as a community to raise critical funds to defy cancer.

img.alt_text: A pediatric cancer patient smiling and holding a cookie

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rally Against CancerTM
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Opening Day at Fenway Park, Red Sox and Jimmy Fund fans celebrated by forming Rally Against CancerTM teams in their workplaces, schools, and communities, and raised $270,000 to defy cancer. Fisher Elementary of Walpole, Mass., and Northwestern Mutual Boston were the top fundraisers in a field of 52 Rally…

Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

For 27 years, Swim Across America has supported Dana-Farber through events like their annual Boston Open Water Swim event. In 2022, swimmers of all ages and skill levels raised $142,000 to help support cancer research and care at the Institute, for a lifetime total of more than $3 million.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Swim Across America
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Swim Across America hosted their 28th annual Boston Open Water Swim event, which directly benefits Dana-Farber patients and families. Swimmers of all ages and skills levels united to “Make Waves Against Cancer” and raised $175,000, bringing the event’s cumulative fundraising total to over $3 million to date.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Swim Across America
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Swim Across America raised $250,000 in 2024 to benefit Dana-Farber’s Perini Family Survivors’ Center. Since 1996, the Boston Open Water Swim has united swimmers of all ages and abilities, raising over $3.5 million in total to support vital survivorship research at Dana-Farber and continuing to “Make Waves Against Cancer.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Swim Across America
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Swim Across America’s Boston Open Water Swim raised $335,000 in 2025 to benefit patients who receive care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and their families. Raising over $3.8 million since 1996, the organization continues to “Make Waves to Fight Cancer” and fuel critical survivorship research at Dana-Farber. This year's event will…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Friends of Dana-Farber hosted a variety of events throughout 2024 that raised more than $600,000 for lifesaving cancer research and patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach surpasses $67 million in gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over three decades, the compassionate community in Palm Beach, Florida, has provided generous support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s lifesaving mission to conquer cancer in adults and children—not only in Boston and Palm Beach, but also across the country and around the world.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber Palm Beach Campaign Leadership Celebration Dinner

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rybacki Memorial surpasses $1 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thirty years ago, 16 golfers in the first Rybacki Memorial Golf Tournament raised $1,200 for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. In 2022, 150 golfers raised more than $145,000

img.alt_text: Larry and Chris Rybacki pose for a photo while golfing

Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Bryce Vickmark 

James W. Ware left a generous gift of $334,745 to provide unrestricted support for research and care at Dana-Farber. Unrestricted gifts provide flexible support for programs throughout Dana-Farber, from innovative basic research, to clinical trials, to programs that enhance the Institute’s signature Total Patient Care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Unrestricted support: A powerful vote of confidence
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Campaign is a catalyst for giving at every level, including through the Defy Cancer Fund, and has inspired tremendous unrestricted support from our generous philanthropic community.

img.alt_text: An image of a scientist looking through a test tube (image has blue overlay)

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Our historic partner, the Dana Foundation, made a new $100,000 commitment to the Defy Cancer Fund, which provides unrestricted support for The Dana-Farber Campaign. These flexible funds propel innovative early stage research, speed new drugs into clinical trials, retain and attract top talent; meet unanticipated needs; and ensure that we…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Anthony Sordillo leaves legacy of generosity
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Former Dana-Farber anesthesiologist Anthony Sordillo left a generous unrestricted bequest to advance our lifesaving mission.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The success of our mission hinges on unrestricted gifts, including those raised through the Defy Cancer Fund.

jetpack-related-posts.title: TA Associates
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: TA Associates made a generous, unrestricted gift of $170,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Their vital support empowers the Institute to advance cancer research and patient care, fostering innovation and expanding access to treatment. TA's flexible commitment plays a crucial role in driving progress and improving outcomes for patients and families.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Crystal Family Charitable Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Crystal Family Charitable Foundation recently made a generous $200,000 gift to support a variety of research and patient care programs at Dana-Farber. The funds will drive innovative prostate and pancreatic cancer research while enhancing social services offered to pediatric patients and grieving families.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Unpaved
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PMC Unpaved is a gravel bike ride over the scenic backroads of the Berkshires in western Massachusetts that raises funds for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

img.alt_text: A group of bicycle riders riding along a wooded path

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ravestock Boston
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Ravestock Boston, hosted in October by the William Raveis Charitable Fund, raised nearly $150,000 for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s life-changing mission. Held in memory of Meghan Raveis, the event brought together community and live music to benefit Dana-Farber's cancer research and care, while honoring Meghan’s legacy of service to others.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jog for Julie
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 7th annual Jog for Julie fundraiser, held in honor of a breast cancer patient, raised more than $30,000 in 2022. The 5K was started in 2014 by Julie’s entire family, including her four children, and has raised more than $220,000 for breast cancer research at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Keep Smiling Beautiful
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Keep Smiling Beautiful is a 5K race hosted by the family of Chelsea Smith, to champion research into hepatocellular carcinoma—liver cancer—by Chelsea’s doctor, Allison O’Neill, MD, at Dana-Farber. Each year, in Chelsea’s honor, O’Neill runs this 5K which has raised more than $115,000 since 2017.

img.alt_text: An image of a photo collage with balloons

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ang’s Warrior Walk
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 2023, the annual Ang’s Warrior Walk has raised $100,000 for the Angela Marotta Inho Memorial Fund, which supports lung cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Organized by Jennifer and Allison Inho, Founders of the Angela Marotta Inho Foundation, the event honors their mother Angela, who received care at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: The Inho's standing next to a sponsor banner

jetpack-related-posts.title: William and Barbara Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Sara M. Tolaney, MD, MPH, received a $100,000 gift from the Connolly Family Fund, established by William and Barbara Connolly, to advance innovative breast cancer research. Their support empowers Tolaney’s team to develop novel strategies for early detection, prevention, and personalized treatment, helping to improve outcomes for…

title.rendered: Dana-Farber joins with Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy to accelerate cures for the world’s gravest cancers

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy and Robin Orwant

Dana-Farber has partnered with the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy (PICI), the leading network of immuno-oncology expertise in the world, as a member of the PICI Network with a goal of better understanding the tumor microenvironment across cancer types and translating these basic discoveries into impactful cancer immunotherapies for patients.

The PICI Network was established to promote collaboration between leading-edge research institutions in the field of cancer immunology. Encouraging interdisciplinary collaboration and sharing research advances enables the network to maximize the scientific value of discoveries and catalyze the development of more effective cancer immunotherapies.

Funding for centers in the PICI Network supports bold, high-risk scientific research that bridges academia and biotech through the potential formation of companies founded to develop next-generation cancer therapies. PICI also facilitates access to advanced bioinformatics, intellectual property, sequencing, immune monitoring, industry-owned drugs, cell manufacturing, genetic engineering, and clinical trial management. Network institutes also are offered resources to develop the next generation of scientific leaders as part of PICI’s Early Career Researchers program.

“Dana-Farber investigators are innovators in immuno-oncology,” said Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, Dana-Farber president and CEO and the Richard and Susan Smith Professor of Medicine. “As an institutional member of the PICI Network, we will expand our opportunities to work jointly with fellow leaders in the field, bringing together a powerful combination of expertise and resources that will significantly augment our impact on patients.”

Among multiple other research pursuits, scientists at Dana-Farber are drawing a clearer picture of how tumor microenvironments change in response to immunotherapy. The researchers believe this work points to potential targets for the development of more effective drug therapies.

The Center is led by Co-Directors F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, who also directs the Melanoma Center and the Center for Immuno-Oncology and is the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber; Elizabeth Mittendorf, MD, PhD, director of Dana-Farber’s Breast Immuno-oncology Program and co-director of the Breast Cancer Clinical Research Program; and Kai Wucherpfennig, MD, PhD, chair of Cancer Immunology and Virology and director of the Center for Cancer Immunotherapy Research at Dana-Farber, and the Nancy Lurie Marks Professor of Neurology in the Field of Medical Oncology. The PICI grant supports The Dana-Farber Campaign, Dana-Farber’s ambitious, multi-year fundraising effort to prevent, treat, and defy cancer by accelerating revolutionary science, extraordinary care, exceptional expertise, and essential opportunities.

“As a PICI Network member, Dana-Farber will be an even more integral part of a national and international team of scientists working in concert to deliver cures to patients.”

John Connolly, PHD, Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy

As PICI Network collaborators since 2017, Dana-Farber researchers already have contributed to high-profile PICI cancer research studies, including the AMADEUS, REVOLUTION, and PRINCE clinical trials; TRIBUTE, a data-driven approach to metastatic triple-negative breast cancer; the Tumor Neoantigen Selection Alliance; and the revolutionary discovery of a cancer detection protein in the immune system.

“As a PICI Network member, Dana-Farber will be an even more integral part of a national and international team of scientists working in concert to deliver cures to patients,” said John Connolly, PhD, PICI chief scientific officer. “We welcome the progression of our partnership and look forward to even greater collaboration ahead.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: CRI grants accelerate immunotherapy research at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Research Institute (CRI) is advancing bold new strategies to harness the immune system against cancer through two grants at DanaFarber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Mark Foundation spurs innovation in immunotherapy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research has awarded Dana-Farber investigator Catherine Wu, MD, and two investigators at the Broad Institute a $3 million, three-year grant to further their research into personalized, T cell-directed cancer immunotherapy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prevention is goal of groundbreaking immunotherapy trial
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When asked what motivates her to support cancer research, Susan Hertog starts at the beginning, when her best friend was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer at the age of 49.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cancer Research Institute invests in the people behind basic research discoveries in cancer immunology
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: While the immune system is inherently able to identify and destroy harmful cells, tumors often develop ways to interrupt anti-cancer immune activity. Restoring this powerful effect in order to defeat cancer through therapies that galvanize the immune system has transformed the treatment trajectory and potential for cure in many cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding in 2007, the Melanoma Research Alliance has become the largest nonprofit funder of crucial melanoma research worldwide. In 2025, they awarded $430,000 in grants to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporting the work of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD, Giacomo Oliveira, PhD, and David Liu, MD, MPH, MS, to advance…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Belfers aim to make immunotherapy effective for more patients
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: An extraordinary gift of $10 million from Robert and Renée Belfer and family will support innovative immuno-oncology research at Dana-Farber.

title.rendered: Jimmy Fund Golf celebrates 40 years of defying cancer from the fairways

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Shannon Watterson

Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun returned in full force in 2022, with courses around New England and across the country welcoming golfers in support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund’s lifesaving mission. Thanks to dedicated volunteer tournament directors, sponsors, donors, and players, Jimmy Fund Golf raised more than $6.7 million through more than 140 golf events in 2022 to help Dana-Farber defy cancer.

Making this year extra special was the celebration of Jimmy Fund Golf’s 40th season. Since the program was officially formed in 1983 by a small group of passionate golfers and fundraisers—some of whom are still involved today—Jimmy Fund Golf has grown into a committed community united in its efforts to create a world without cancer. Contributing more than $156 million to cancer care and research, this golf community has been instrumental in advancing Dana-Farber’s revolutionary work, and Jimmy Fund Golf looks forward to another 40 years together on the fairways.

Find full coverage of Jimmy Fund Golf’s 2022 season, including photos, leaderboard, milestone anniversaries, and sponsors, in The Year in Review.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun marked another ace year in 2023, with an array of dedicated tournament directors, sponsors, and supporters across the country raising more than $6.8 million for The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella plays an MVP role in the Jimmy Fund’s mission to strike out cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund, Arbella Insurance Group continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber’s mission throughout 2023, living out the company’s motto of: “Here. For Good.”

img.alt_text: A group of people holding an over-sized check at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: An un-fore-gettable year with Jimmy Fund Golf
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun raised $6.8 million in 2024, thanks to organizers and participants in more than 140 events across the country.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Another ace year for Jimmy Fund Golf
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun raised $6.8 million in 2024, thanks to organizers and participants in more than 140 events across the country.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Jimmy Fund celebrates 75 years
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 22, 1948, Einar Gustafson, a young boy being treated for lymphoma by Dr. Sidney Farber and dubbed “Jimmy” to protect his privacy, shared his story from his hospital bed.

img.alt_text: The original Jimmy in a hospital bed with an old TV

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expect Miracles Foundation honored with the Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Expect Miracles Foundation (EMF) received the 2025 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award—the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor—during a special on-field ceremony at Fenway Park.

title.rendered: Physician pioneer in palliative care establishes a research fellowship

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Stephanie Lowitt
Photography by Sam Ogden

In 2001, Janet L. Abrahm, MD, joined Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as a palliative care physician, becoming a pivotal force in founding and nurturing the Adult Palliative Care Program—a move that created a sea change in how Dana-Farber cares for patients with cancer and brought much-deserved attention and recognition to the field. Palliative care physicians ensure patients with serious illness maintain their best quality of life and manage physical symptoms by identifying what matters most to patients—essentially aligning care plans with individual values.

Today, Dana-Farber, is one of the few cancer centers that has an integrated Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care Department. As a national leader, Abrahm understood the importance of supporting patients’ emotional well-being through the uncertain journey of cancer treatment and survivorship. Now, Abrahm is once again elevating this important discipline by providing opportunities for the next generation of professionals by establishing a Research Fellowship.  A pioneer professionally and philanthropically, Abrahm decided to provide annual support to establish and sustain the fellowship during her lifetime while ensuring it lasts in perpetuity by endowing the fund with a $1 million bequest.

This fellowship is a generous and significant tribute to the life work of Abrahm and her dedication to Dana-Farber’s core value of compassionate care. Throughout her career, Abrahm has mentored countless physicians and tirelessly supported the growth of Dana-Farber’s nationally recognized department. This fellowship will sustain that work and allow Dana-Farber to attract the brightest early career palliative care clinician-researchers and grow the next generation.

“I am overwhelmed with gratitude for Janet’s generosity and thoughtfulness,” says James Tulsky, MD, chair of the department of Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care, and the Poorvu Jaffe Chair in Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care at Dana-Farber. “She is one of our field’s great pioneers, and her dedication to patients and to the Division of Adult Palliative Care over the last 20 years is unmatched. This gift exemplifies her commitment to the Institute’s mission and to advancing the science and practice of palliative care. It is an honor to partner with Janet in considering her legacy.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leadership gift establishes Poorvu Jaffe Chair in Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care and launches health equity initiative
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber is committed to providing the best possible care to patients from all walks of life. In recent years, the Institute has prioritized expanding its clinical facilities into surrounding communities to better reach medically underserved patients with the Institute’s signature Total Patient Care model, which includes supportive services from the…

img.alt_text: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and Daniel G. Jaffe

jetpack-related-posts.title: Poorvu Jaffe Chair Celebration
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: James Tulsky, MD, was named the first incumbent of the Poorvu Jaffe Chair in Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care at Dana-Farber, the first chair in this field established at the Institute. The Poorvu Jaffe Family’s gift also established the Poorvu Jaffe Fund for Supportive Oncology and Health Equity. Pictured at…

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Academy of Neurology Institute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Academy of Neurology Institute provided $150,000 to support the clinical research of Dana-Farber neurooncologist and palliative care specialist John Rhee, MD, MPH. The funds will help accelerate his work elevating care standards and developing therapeutic strategies that are better-tolerated than current options for glioma patients.

img.alt_text: Steaming beaker and pipette in the lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: A legacy of care: Elevating palliative nursing education
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Shannon Robins and her husband, Jason Robins, co-founder and CEO of DraftKings, a Jimmy Fund corporate sponsor, made a visionary $1 million gift to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, helping to launch a first-of-its-kind palliative care education program designed by nurses, for nurses.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Christine Brown
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Christine A. Brown Research Fellowship Fund at Dana-Farber was recently established with a $160,000 gift from Christine Brown. The fund will benefit the Department of Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care, allowing investigators to conduct studies that seek to improve quality of life at every stage of a patient’s cancer…

img.alt_text: Various tubes and other lab equipment

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Palliative Care Research Center
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The National Palliative Care Research Center awarded $198,000 to support the creation of a program to develop nurse-led psychosocial intervention for historically marginalized pediatric patients, with the goal of improving family-centered communication and pediatric patients’ quality of life during treatment.

title.rendered: Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation grants millions to advance childhood cancer research

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Jodi Hyer
Photography by Sam Ogden  

It all began over 20 years ago with a simple, yet profound, act of kindness by Alex Scott, a determined little girl with cancer, who held a lemonade stand fundraiser to help other kids like her and inspired countless others to do the same. Since her passing at the age of 8, Alex’s legacy of kindness and determination has continued through Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation (ALSF), which has awarded more than 1,000 research grants to 150+ institutions in North America in pursuit of her vision—a cure for all children with cancer.

ALSF recently awarded grants totaling $3.32 million to advance the Institute’s pediatric oncology research efforts, bringing the total granted to Dana-Farber physician-scientists to over $19 million since 2005. Rani George, MD, PhD, leading a group of researchers from four other institutions, received a $3 million award as part of ALSF’s Crazy 8 Initiative aimed at curing hard-to-treat cancers. George and her co-investigators will identify and target genetic drivers of osteosarcoma lung metastasis, the primary cause of death in osteosarcoma. This research will leverage cutting-edge technologies to investigate genetic changes in individual cancer cells as metastasis develops and to develop new drugs acting as “molecular glues” to stick to target proteins involved in metastatic disease causing them to be destroyed inside the cell. Such new therapies would be a milestone for metastatic osteosarcoma, which has not seen treatment improvements in decades. George also received an Innovation Award to test a novel compound that may target the synthesis of a protein called MYCN, which is critical for uncontrolled cancer cell growth in MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma.

ALSF gave Young Investigator Awards to Riaz Gillani, MD, and John Prensner, MD, PhD. Gillani will use his funding to study the role of inherited mutations, including those involved in DNA damage repair, in the development of neuroblastoma and to identify specific mutations associated with high-risk neuroblastoma, which is the most difficult to treat. Prensner will explore how a newly identified protein, ASNSD1 uORF, and other proteins derived from un-mapped regions of the “dark genome” are regulated by and work in conjunction with MYC, a well-known genetic driver of medulloblastoma.

ALSF also made four grants to fund pediatric oncology student research projects, supporting the Institute’s commitment in training the next generation of oncology researchers. ALSF co-executive director Liz Scott shared, “My daughter Alex left a legacy that has allowed us to change the lives of other children with cancer and their families. These grants represent our continued commitment to funding the most promising scientists and ideas that will lead to new cures for all children with cancer.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation continues steadfast support
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The legacy of a remarkable little girl has guided the mission of Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation (ALSF) since it was established in 2005.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation targets childhood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2000, a 4-year-old girl named Alexandra “Alex” Scott set up a lemonade stand to raise money for research into childhood cancers like hers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jog for Julie
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 7th annual Jog for Julie fundraiser, held in honor of a breast cancer patient, raised more than $30,000 in 2022. The 5K was started in 2014 by Julie’s entire family, including her four children, and has raised more than $220,000 for breast cancer research at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Meghan McCarthy Fund marks milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Meghan McCarthy Research Fund surpassed $1 million in funding to support glioblastoma research at Dana-Farber in memory of a high school athlete and Jimmy Fund fundraiser who passed away in 2010.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kicks for Cancer celebrates record-setting year
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year since 2007, Kicks for Cancer has brought together athletes and fans from Concord-Carlisle High School and 17 surrounding towns to raise funds for ovarian cancer research at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Young soccer players in bright pink shirts

jetpack-related-posts.title: OOFOS surpasses $4 million milestone in 2024 to advance breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For nearly a decade, OOFOS has supported breast cancer research at Dana-Farber through its Project Pink initiative.

title.rendered: Edward P. Evans Foundation grants propel MDS research

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Scott Edwards
Photography by Sam Ogden

The Edward P. Evans Foundation, which funds the most promising research in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), a type of blood cancer, has awarded grants totaling $2.325 million to five Dana-Farber researchers who are pursuing innovative MDS strategies.

As director of the Edward P. Evans Center for MDS at Dana-Farber, R. Coleman Lindsley, MD, PhD, is investigating the role of telomere dysfunction in MDS. Telomeres are caps at the end of each strand of DNA that protect chromosomes. Lindsley previously reported that inherited defects in the maintenance of telomeres are linked to MDS and that patients who have short telomeres have poor survival after bone marrow transplantation. This new funding will support improved clinical testing, influence treatment decisions, and aid in the design of new therapies for patients with MDS.

“I am grateful for the Evans Foundation’s support of this research. An improved understanding of how telomere damage influences development and treatment of MDS may further inform prognosis and drive the discovery of better treatment approaches,” said Lindsley.

With her grant, Zuzana Tothova, MD, PhD, is using research models of cohesin-mutant MDS to study the role of inflammation during disease development. Mutations in the cohesin protein complex occur in up to 20% of MDS. She will also investigate whether reactivating transposable elements, fragments of DNA inserted into our germline from ancient viral infection, drives MDS inflammatory changes, which could aid in developing new treatments.

Philipp Rauch, MD, is using barcoding technology to track blood cells to understand how the behavior of cells carrying a mutation for clonal hematopoiesis, an MDS precursor condition, differs from that of normal cells, which may help identify new therapeutic targets.

Previously, Rahul Vedula, MD, found that MDS cells carrying a specific mutation in the U2AF1 gene often have a mutation in the BCOR gene as well. He is studying the molecular mechanisms by which the two genes cooperate to drive MDS.

Hypomethylating agents are cornerstone treatments for MDS, but their anti-tumor mechanisms remain poorly understood. Rishi Puram, MD, PhD, is investigating epigenetic mechanisms that modulate cellular responses to hypomethylating agents, which may offer insight into new therapies that target DNA methylation in MDS.

“We are grateful for the talent, dedication, and commitment of our supported Dana-Farber investigators to finding solutions to the complex challenge of MDS, and we are proud to support their work,” said Michael Lewis, president of the Edward P. Evans Foundation.

The funding supports two early career researchers pursuing projects that seek to deepen our understanding of the tumor microenvironment and develop cutting-edge strategies to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research awarded $250,000 to Dana-Farber’s Zuzana Tothova, MD, PhD, who is exploring the biology of cohesin mutations, frequent and recurrent drivers of myelodysplastic syndromes and acute myeloid leukemia. With this funding, Tothova aims to develop targeted treatments for these cancers.

title.rendered: Endowed chair honors the legacy of David Livingston, MD

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Caitlin Henault
Photography by Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Getty Images

In 2021, the world lost a giant of cancer medicine with the sudden passing of David Livingston, MD. An internationally recognized cancer biologist, Livingston was a renowned expert on the molecular origins of breast and ovarian cancer. Livingston was the Charles A. Dana Chair in Human Cancer Genetics at Dana-Farber and the Emil Frei III, MD, Distinguished Professor of Genetics and Medicine at Harvard Medical School at the time of his death.

Livingston’s research focused on genes that regulate cell growth in the body, and his work has been the cornerstone of many studies of cancer susceptibility linked to BRCA function and mutations. By understanding the tumor suppressive properties of BRCA1 and BRCA2, he paved the way for studying novel approaches to breast and ovarian cancer prevention.

Livingston held numerous leadership positions at Dana-Farber and emphasized collaboration as foundational to major discoveries, including the Bridge Project, which links the cancer research efforts of the Koch Institute for Integrative Research at MIT and Dana-Farber/Harvard Cancer Center. Above all, Livingston served as a valuable mentor, taking more than 200 students, fellows, and junior scientists under his wing throughout his 50-year career at Dana-Farber.

“David was one of the world’s leading scientists, but that only scratches the surface of why he is missed,” said Dana-Farber’s William G. Kaelin Jr., MD, a 2019 Nobel laureate and the Sidney Farber, MD, Professor of Medicine. “David served as my mentor since I first entered his laboratory, where I was immediately inspired by his intellect and infectious enthusiasm. He continued to support me and so many others throughout our careers.”

In an outpouring of support, nearly 200 of his family members, friends, colleagues, collaborators, past trainees, Dana-Farber Trustees, donors, and grant-makers contributed more than $3 million to endow the David M. Livingston, MD, Chair at Dana-Farber in his honor.

“We think that David would appreciate being recognized in this meaningful way,” said Dana-Farber Trustees Debbie and Bob First. “David was responsible for Debbie’s treatment for ovarian cancer in 1977— and why she is here today. We all miss his genius and his humor, but mostly we miss his friendship.”

“We are pleased to support the future scientific accomplishments of this new chair in memory of David, who was a monumental figure in cancer research,” said Caroline Montojo, president and CEO of the Dana Foundation.

“We’ll never be able to replace David’s presence, but this endowed chair honors him by ensuring patients everywhere continue to benefit from his extraordinary legacy.”

William G. Kaelin Jr., MD

Pasi Jänne, MD, PhD, director of the Robert and Renée Belfer Center for Applied Cancer Science, the Carole M. and Philip L. Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology, and the Chen-Huang Center for EGFR-Mutant Lung Cancers at Dana-Farber, will serve as the inaugural incumbent of the David M. Livingston, MD, Chair at Dana-Farber.

“We are proud to support this endowed chair to honor David’s legacy, enabling his spirit of mentorship, scholarly research, and collaboration to continue,” said Mindy and Jon Gray of the Gray Foundation, who contributed a gift of $1 million to seed this chair in Livingston’s memory.

Added Kaelin: “We’ll never be able to replace David’s presence, but this endowed chair honors him by supporting the work of a leading cancer scientist in perpetuity and ensuring patients everywhere continue to benefit from his extraordinary legacy.”

title.rendered: Milestone 20th annual WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon raises $3.5 million

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Michael Quinn
Photography by John Deputy

Since 1953, the Boston Red Sox have had a deep and multifaceted impact on patients with cancer through the team’s strong partnership with Dana-Farber the team’s the Jimmy Fund. A shining example of this is the WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance, the yearly fundraiser through which the Red Sox have pitched in to strike out this disease since 2002.

Taking place on August 23 and 24, 2022 at Fenway Park, the 20th annual Radio-Telethon generated over $3.5 million for adult and pediatric cancer research and care at Dana-Farber, bringing the program’s cumulative total to $65 million since 2002. This strong team effort was propelled by gifts from the Red Sox Partners Challenge, NESN employee fundraising and company match, and generous contributions from Rob Hale, Ernie Boch Jr., Rockport Mortgage, and the Arbella Insurance Foundation. Once again, WEEI and NESN executed an outstanding 36-hour broadcast that featured stories from Dana-Farber doctors, patients, and families, bolstered by special appearances by Red Sox executives, players, coaches, and alumni, as well as sports heroes and leaders from the Patriots, Bruins, and Celtics, plus other special guests.

As always, the Radio-Telethon abounded with memorable moments that moved the hearts of listeners and viewers alike. Especially inspiring were segments featuring patients, who shared hopeful stories and shined in on-field ceremonies to commemorate the milestone anniversary. Several patients from past Radio-Telethons returned this year, including Tori Rando and Tanya Searle, who first became close friends as teen patients in Dana-Farber’s Jimmy Fund Clinic; Vinny Basile, who was also treated at the clinic as a teen and celebrated his 39th birthday at the 2022 broadcast; clinic patient Ben Finer, who graduated college in 2020 and now works in tech support; and OK Eason, who is still cycling and going strong thanks to an experimental treatment at Dana-Farber that keeps his glioblastoma at bay. All embody the powerful possibilities unlocked by advances enabled through funding from the Radio-Telethon.

Radio-Telethon’s success is due in part to the continued commitment of presenting sponsor, Arbella Insurance. John Donohue, chairman, president, and CEO of the Arbella Insurance Group and chairman of the Arbella Insurance Foundation, underscored the Radio-Telethon’s importance to Arbella and the communities it serves: “The Radio-Telethon shows how many people are touched by cancer and reminds us about the great work being done by the doctors, nurses, and staff at Dana-Farber. Arbella is extremely proud to support Dana-Farber in its work to treat and help prevent this devastating disease.”

From left: Tori Rando, Vinny Basile, and Tanya Searle; OK Eason (left) with his neuro-oncologist, David Reardon, MD.; Ben Finer.

excerpt.rendered: Since 1953, the Boston Red Sox have had a deep and multifaceted impact on patients with cancer through its strong partnership with Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund.

jetpack-related-posts.title: WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon surpasses $70 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to thousands of generous supporters from across the country, the 21st annual WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance raised more than $4 million.

img.alt_text: A participant in the Jimmy Fund Radio Telethon

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella Insurance Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Special thanks to our friends at Arbella Insurance Foundation, which is making a $50 contribution for each strikeout thrown by a Boston Red Sox pitcher up to $100,000 in total. This promotion has raised more than $1.1 million since 2014 while amplifying Arbella Insurance’s impact as a longstanding Dana-Farber supporter…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Chairmen of the Jimmy Fund: building community since 1948
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since the earliest days of the Jimmy Fund, passionate and committed individuals have devoted their time, talents, resources, and relationships to raising money in support of a powerful possibility: curing cancer for everyone.

img.alt_text: Larry Lucchino at the Boston Marathon Jimmy Fund Walk

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon breaks records with $5.7 million raised for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance continued to be a beacon of support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in August with a record-breaking fundraising year.

img.alt_text: Ali Kelleher cheering at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Another home run year for the Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance helped strike out cancer for the 22nd year at Fenway Park in August, raising nearly $4 million for adult and pediatric cancer care and research at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expect Miracles Foundation honored with the Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Expect Miracles Foundation (EMF) received the 2025 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award—the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor—during a special on-field ceremony at Fenway Park.
